body: Linux quick gate on head f4c70ab7 (base issue/819-fixture-plates): green - app suites ok (178 s), ui suites ok (60 s), 0 failed, wall 4.0 min. Local: clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings clean.

Review blocker fixed on head 5920a084 (`fix(app): a plate edit never pushes a mod vise jaw into the stock`, Refs #820). The PR stays a draft.

**Changes**
- **`SetPlate` refuses a plate edit that puts a mod vise jaw into the stock.** The check names the block, its side and the depth: "the plate edit would put mod vise '...''s adjustable jaw 16.000 mm into the stock - re-place the pair after changing the grid". It measures in the block's own frame against the stock box, the same box the fit uses (`modvise::reach::face_gap`). It refuses when the edit puts a face into the stock or deeper. When an edit lifts a face off the stock, that is a warning, not a refusal; re-fitting the slide stays in #832.
- **`SetPlate` now clash-checks every fixture it re-seats, and the plate's new slab, the way `MoveFixture` does.** It checks against parts and stock (`fixture_clash::after_fixture_shape`). The warning comes back by name (`SetPlate::warning`, MCP `set_fixture_plate` -> `warning`). **This also closes the same gap for plain riders from #823.** #823 is merge-ready and takes no pushes, so the fix lives here. The PR body now says so.
- The status line after placing a pair gives the slide in document units (`crates/ui/src/state_modvise.rs`).
- Decision file: added notes on plate edits vs. the stock, and that `body_height` must cover the bolt heads (counterbored bolts).

**Pins** (each one fails with the new checks removed)
- `mod_vise_plate::a_plate_edit_that_pushes_a_jaw_into_the_stock_is_refused_by_name`: the review's rig (60 mm stock, 770MX plate, 1 in preset, fixed C14, adjustable I16, slide 22.55). Pitch Y - 2 is refused naming the adjustable block, 16.000 mm. Pitch Y + 2 is refused naming the fixed block, 4.000 mm.
- `mod_vise_plate::a_plate_edit_that_keeps_the_jaws_clear_is_accepted_and_undoes_exactly`: pitch X + 0.2 is accepted with no warning. Undo and redo restore the poses exactly, to the bit. A refused edit leaves nothing behind.
- `fixture_plate_riders::an_edited_plates_riders_are_clash_checked_where_they_land`: a plain rider re-seated 4 mm into the stock gets the warning by name. A clear edit gives no warning. Undo and redo are exact.
- `fixture_modvise_tests::the_placed_status_states_the_slide_in_document_units` (ui; the mm case is also asserted in the existing placement test).

**Gate**
- Local (macOS, private target dir), all green: app `mod_vise`, `mod_vise_plate`, `mcp_mod_vise`, `fixture_plate`, `fixture_plate_riders`, `commands_undo`, `mcp_plate`, `fixture_plate_detect`; ui `--lib fixture` (33 passed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Linux quick gate (base `issue/819-fixture-plates`): green. App suites 169 s, ui suites 50 s, 0 failed.

@mkinney This conflicts with main. Please run `git merge origin/main` on `issue/820-mod-vises` and push. It touches the same fixture files as #823 (`crates/app/src/commands/*fixture*.rs`, `crates/app/src/project/*`, `crates/app/src/mcp/*`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_*`, `crates/ui/src/state*.rs`). Around 24 hunks, so please resolve by hand and keep both sides where both sides added lines.
Back to draft: it conflicts with main, so a merge of main is being pushed (a ready PR takes no pushes).

Merged #823's fixed branch (issue/819-fixture-plates, which already carries main) into this one (FixtureDef, project wire and lenient load, state, module lists: keep both sides; the mod-jaw key keeps its drop-and-log read inside fixture_keys). Targeted gate: quick on app suites green; ui lib suite green; clippy -D warnings clean on camcraft-app and camcraft-ui. One unrelated item: gpu_render docs_images_match_the_rendered_steps shows pixel drift on a Linux run (files this PR does not touch). Ready for a re-check (/resolve-conflicts check). It was ready before, so it stays a draft until the re-check, then flag it ready.
